title: What Arcology Towers Is
definition: Arcology Towers: self-contained vertical cities housing millions per tower.
description:
Arcology Towers — Signature Edition: self-contained vertical cities housing millions per tower. This is the JAH-original vision, designed from first principles and labeled as Signature speculation throughout.

The Signature tower hulls program starts where public roadmaps stop. Where public research asks what is fundable, the Signature line asks what is buildable: stacked districts rethought, vertical transit rebuilt, sky infrastructure reimagined for the century ahead. Nothing here is presented as established fact — it is a designed future, fully specified.

This edition mirrors the public database record for record — concept, components, milestones, demos, drills, alliance, roadmap — but every entry is the Signature take: bolder timelines, integrated systems thinking, and the residential layers ambition that defines the Signature line.

title: The Signature Vision: Arcology Towers
definition: The JAH-original Signature vision of Arcology Towers.
description:
The Signature vision of Arcology Towers does not ask what committees will fund — it asks what physics allows and what engineering can compound.

Signature tower hulls program, charter one: master stacked districts at laboratory scale within the decade. Charter two: scale vertical transit manufacturing until cost collapses. Charter three: operate sky infrastructure systems continuously, learning in public, improving every cycle.

This is a Signature concept — original JAH speculation, fully specified and honestly labeled. The public edition of this database carries the documented research record; this edition carries the bolder integrated vision: what Arcology Towers becomes when every piece is designed to work with every other piece from day one.

title: The tower hulls Grid
definition: The tower hulls Grid: a load-bearing component of Arcology Towers.
description:
The urban backbone: power, water, data and logistics woven into one stacked districts grid that the tower hulls district runs on.

In the Arcology Towers architecture, the tower hulls grid is load-bearing: without it the tower hulls fails outright — Arcology Towers stops being Arcology Towers at all. Builders sequence this piece early because every other component assumes it works. In the Signature architecture this piece is designed first-class, not bolted on.

Maturity varies: some deployments of this piece exist today in simpler forms, while the full Arcology Towers-grade version remains a research target. The readiness estimator in this database scores it honestly.

t: 2030 — The first tower hulls district opens at 50
title: 2030 — The first tower hulls district opens at 50
definition: 2030 milestone on the Arcology Towers roadmap.
description:
The first tower hulls district opens at 50,000 residents, its stacked districts grid and vertical transit mobility running at full design load.

What must be true first: the stacked districts results have to replicate outside the lab, vertical transit manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and sky infrastructure operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting. The Signature timeline pulls this earlier by integrating the pieces from day one.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed stacked districts demonstrations, vertical transit cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting sky infrastructure uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Arcology Towers
definition: Estimates Arcology Towers readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Arcology Towers components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a tower hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Arcology Towers Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Arcology Towers operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Arcology Towers installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 12142 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where stacked districts monitoring, vertical transit redundancy, or sky infrastructure maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Arcology Towers Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Arcology Towers: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Arcology Towers — self-contained vertical cities housing millions per tower.

Phase 1 — Prove (stacked districts): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (vertical transit): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (sky infrastructure): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (residential layers): tower hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and urban core-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.

Each phase has exit criteria.
Unites all 20 records.
